    21→def parse_freedesktop_os_release(content):
    22→    """Parse the content of an /etc/os-release file.
    23→
    24→    Implementation adapted from Example 5 of
    25→    https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/os-release.html
    26→
    27→    :param content: The text content of the /etc/os-release file.
    28→    :returns: A dictionary of key-value pairs, in the same format returned by
    29→        `platform.freedesktop_os_release()`.
    30→    """
    31→    values = {}
    32→    for line_number, line in enumerate(content.split("\n"), start=1):
    33→        line = line.rstrip()
    34→        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
    35→            continue
    36→        m = re.match(r"([A-Z][A-Z_0-9]+)=(.*)", line)
    37→        if m:
    38→            name, val = m.groups()
    39→            if val and val[0] in "\"'":
    40→                try:
    41→                    val = ast.literal_eval(val)
    42→                except SyntaxError as e:
    43→                    raise ParseError(
    44→                        "Failed to parse output of FreeDesktop os-release file; "
    45→                        f"Line {line_number}: {e}"
    46→                    )
    47→            values[name] = val
    48→        else:
    49→            raise ParseError(
    50→                "Failed to parse output of FreeDesktop os-release file; "
    51→                f"Line {line_number}: {line!r}"
    52→            )
    53→
    54→    return values

    83→    def vendor_details(self, freedesktop_info):
    84→        """Normalize the identity of the target Linux vendor, version, and base.
    85→
    86→        :param freedesktop_info: The parsed content of the FreeDesktop /etc/os-release
    87→            file. This is the same format returned by
    88→            `platform.freedesktop_os_release()`.
    89→        :returns: A tuple of (vendor, version, vendor_base).
    90→        """
    91→        vendor = freedesktop_info["ID"]
    92→        try:
    93→            codename = freedesktop_info["VERSION_CODENAME"]
    94→            if not codename:
    95→                # Fedora *has* a VERSION_CODENAME key, but it is empty.
    96→                # Treat it as missing.
    97→                raise KeyError("VERSION_CODENAME")
    98→        except KeyError:
    99→            try:
   100→                # Arch uses a specific constant in VERSION_ID
   101→                if freedesktop_info["VERSION_ID"] == "TEMPLATE_VERSION_ID":
   102→                    codename = "rolling"
   103→                else:
   104→                    codename = freedesktop_info["VERSION_ID"].split(".")[0]
   105→            except KeyError:
   106→                # Manjaro doesn't have a VERSION_ID key
   107→                codename = "rolling"
   108→
   109→        # Process the vendor_base from the vendor.
   110→        id_like = freedesktop_info.get("ID_LIKE", "").split()
   111→        if vendor == DEBIAN or DEBIAN in id_like or "ubuntu" in id_like:
   112→            vendor_base = DEBIAN
   113→        elif vendor == RHEL or vendor == "fedora" or RHEL in id_like:
   114→            vendor_base = RHEL
   115→        elif vendor == ARCH or ARCH in id_like:
   116→            vendor_base = ARCH
   117→        elif vendor == SUSE or SUSE in id_like:
   118→            vendor_base = SUSE
   119→        else:
   120→            vendor_base = None
   121→
   122→        return vendor, codename, vendor_base

   127→    # as local file references into sdists, and then installing those requirements

   133→    def _install_app_requirements(
   134→        self,
   135→        app: AppConfig,
   136→        requires: List[str],
   137→        app_packages_path: Path,
   138→    ):
   139→        """Install requirements for the app with pip.
   140→
   141→        This method pre-compiles any requirement defined using a local path reference
   142→        into an sdist tarball. This will be used when installing under Docker, as local
   143→        file references can't be accessed in the Docker container.
   144→
   145→        :param app: The app configuration
   146→        :param requires: The list of requirements to install
   147→        :param app_packages_path: The full path of the app_packages folder into which
   148→            requirements should be installed.
   149→        """
   150→        # If we're re-building requirements, purge any pre-existing local
   151→        # requirements.
   152→        local_requirements_path = self.local_requirements_path(app)
   153→        if local_requirements_path.exists():
   154→            self.tools.shutil.rmtree(local_requirements_path)
   155→        self.tools.os.mkdir(local_requirements_path)
   156→
   157→        # Iterate over every requirement, looking for local references
   158→        for requirement in requires:
   159→            if _is_local_requirement(requirement):
   160→                if Path(requirement).is_dir():
   161→                    # Requirement is a filesystem reference
   162→                    # Build an sdist for the local requirement
   163→                    with self.input.wait_bar(f"Building sdist for {requirement}..."):
   164→                        try:
   165→                            self.tools.subprocess.check_output(
   166→                                [
   167→                                    sys.executable,
   168→                                    "-X",
   169→                                    "utf8",
   170→                                    "-m",
   171→                                    "build",
   172→                                    "--sdist",
   173→                                    "--outdir",
   174→                                    local_requirements_path,
   175→                                    requirement,
   176→                                ],
   177→                                encoding="UTF-8",
   178→                            )
   179→                        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
   180→                            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   181→                                f"Unable to build sdist for {requirement}"
   182→                            ) from e
   183→                else:

   189→                            f"Unable to find local requirement {requirement}"
   190→                        ) from e

   192→        # Continue with the default app requirement handling.
   193→        return super()._install_app_requirements(
   194→            app,

   382→    def verify_python(self, app: AppConfig):
   383→        """Verify that the version of Python being used to build the app in Docker is
   384→        compatible with the version being used to run Briefcase.
   385→
   386→        Will raise an exception if the Python version is fundamentally
   387→        incompatible (i.e., if Briefcase doesn't support it); any other version
   388→        discrepancy will log a warning, but continue.
   389→
   390→        Requires that the app tools have been verified.
   391→
   392→        As a side effect of verifying Python, the `python_version_tag` will be
   393→        updated to reflect the *actual* python version, not just a generic "3".
   394→
   395→        :param app: The application being built
   396→        """
   397→        output = self.tools[app].app_context.check_output(
   398→            [
   399→                f"python{app.python_version_tag}",
   400→                "-c",
   401→                (
   402→                    "import sys; "
   403→                    "print(f'{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}')"
   404→                ),
   405→            ]
   406→        )
   407→        # Update the python version tag with the *actual* python version.
   408→        app.python_version_tag = output.split("\n")[0]
   409→        target_python_version = tuple(int(v) for v in app.python_version_tag.split("."))
   410→
   411→        if target_python_version < self.briefcase_required_python_version:
   412→            briefcase_min_version = ".".join(
   413→                str(v) for v in self.briefcase_required_python_version
   414→            )
   415→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   416→                f"The system python3 version provided by {app.target_image} "
   417→                f"is {app.python_version_tag}; Briefcase requires a "
   418→                f"minimum Python3 version of {briefcase_min_version}."
   419→            )
   420→        elif target_python_version != (
   421→            self.tools.sys.version_info.major,
   422→            self.tools.sys.version_info.minor,
   423→        ):
   424→            self.logger.warning(
   425→                f"""
   426→*************************************************************************
   427→** WARNING: Python version mismatch!                                   **
   428→*************************************************************************
   429→
   430→    The system python3 provided by {app.target_image} is {app.python_version_tag}.
   431→    This is not the same as your local system ({self.python_version_tag}).
   432→
   433→    Ensure you have tested for Python version compatibility before
   434→    releasing this app.
   435→
   436→*************************************************************************
   437→"""
   438→            )

   440→    def verify_system_python(self):

   442→        python.
   443→
   444→        Will raise an exception if the system Python isn't an obvious Python3, or the
   445→        Briefcase Python isn't the same version as the system Python.
   446→
   447→        Requires that the app tools have been verified.
   448→        """
   449→        system_python_bin = Path("/usr/bin/python3").resolve()

   451→        if system_version[0] != "python3" or len(system_version) == 1:
   452→            raise BriefcaseCommandError("Can't determine the system python version")

   454→        if system_version[1] != str(self.tools.sys.version_info.minor):
   455→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   456→                f"The version of Python being used to run Briefcase ({self.python_version_tag}) "
   457→                f"is not the system python3 (3.{system_version[1]})."

   460→    def _system_requirement_tools(self, app: AppConfig):
   461→        """Utility method returning the packages and tools needed to verify system
   462→        requirements.
   463→
   464→        :param app: The app being built.
   465→        :returns: A triple containing (0) The list of package names that must
   466→            be installed at a bare minimum; (1) the arguments for the command
   467→            used to verify the existence of a package on a system, and (2)
   468→            the command used to install packages. All three values are `None`
   469→            if the system cannot be identified.
   470→        """
   471→        if app.target_vendor_base == DEBIAN:
   472→            base_system_packages = ["python3-dev", "build-essential"]
   473→            system_verify = ["dpkg", "-s"]
   474→            system_installer = ["apt", "install"]
   475→        elif app.target_vendor_base == RHEL:
   476→            base_system_packages = [
   477→                "python3-devel",
   478→                "gcc",
   479→                "make",
   480→                "pkgconf-pkg-config",
   481→            ]
   482→            system_verify = ["rpm", "-q"]
   483→            system_installer = ["dnf", "install"]
   484→        elif app.target_vendor_base == SUSE:
   485→            base_system_packages = [
   486→                "python3-devel",
   487→                "patterns-devel-base-devel_basis",
   488→            ]
   489→            system_verify = ["rpm", "-q", "--whatprovides"]
   490→            system_installer = ["zypper", "install"]
   491→        elif app.target_vendor_base == ARCH:
   492→            base_system_packages = [
   493→                "python3",
   494→                "base-devel",
   495→            ]
   496→            system_verify = ["pacman", "-Q"]
   497→            system_installer = ["pacman", "-Syu"]
   498→        else:
   499→            base_system_packages = None
   500→            system_verify = None
   501→            system_installer = None
   502→
   503→        return (
   504→            base_system_packages,
   505→            system_verify,
   506→            system_installer,
   507→        )

   509→    def verify_system_packages(self, app: AppConfig):
   510→        """Verify that the required system packages are installed.
   511→
   512→        :param app: The app being built.
   513→        """
   514→        (
   515→            base_system_packages,
   516→            system_verify,
   517→            system_installer,
   518→        ) = self._system_requirement_tools(app)
   519→
   520→        if system_verify is None:
   521→            self.logger.warning(
   522→                """
   523→*************************************************************************
   524→** WARNING: Can't verify system packages                               **
   525→*************************************************************************
   526→
   527→    Briefcase doesn't know how to verify the installation of system
   528→    packages on your Linux distribution. If you have any problems
   529→    building this app, ensure that the packages listed in the app's
   530→    `system_requires` setting have been installed.
   531→
   532→*************************************************************************
   533→"""
   534→            )
   535→            return
   536→
   537→        # Run a check for each package listed in the app's system_requires,
   538→        # plus the baseline system packages that are required.
   539→        missing = []
   540→        for package in base_system_packages + getattr(app, "system_requires", []):
   541→            try:
   542→                self.tools.subprocess.check_output(system_verify + [package])
   543→            except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
   544→                missing.append(package)
   545→
   546→        # If any required packages are missing, raise an error.
   547→        if missing:
   548→            raise BriefcaseCommandError(
   549→                f"""\
   550→Unable to build {app.app_name} due to missing system dependencies. Run:
   551→
   552→    sudo {' '.join(system_installer)} {' '.join(missing)}
   553→
   554→to install the missing dependencies, and re-run Briefcase.
   555→"""
   556→            )

   558→    def verify_app_tools(self, app: AppConfig):
   559→        """Verify App environment is prepared and available.
   560→
   561→        When Docker is used, create or update a Docker image for the App. Without
   562→        Docker, the host machine will be used as the App environment.
   563→
   564→        :param app: The application being built
   565→        """
   566→        # Verifying the App context is idempotent; but we have some
   567→        # additional logic that we only want to run the first time through.
   568→        # Check (and store) the pre-verify app tool state.
   569→        verify_python = not hasattr(self.tools[app], "app_context")
   570→
   571→        if self.use_docker:
   572→            DockerAppContext.verify(
   573→                tools=self.tools,
   574→                app=app,
   575→                image_tag=self.docker_image_tag(app),
   576→                dockerfile_path=self.bundle_path(app) / "Dockerfile",
   577→                app_base_path=self.base_path,
   578→                host_bundle_path=self.bundle_path(app),
   579→                host_data_path=self.data_path,
   580→                python_version=app.python_version_tag,
   581→            )
   582→
   583→            # Check the system Python on the target system to see if it is
   584→            # compatible with Briefcase.
   585→            if verify_python:
   586→                self.verify_python(app)
   587→        else:
   588→            NativeAppContext.verify(tools=self.tools, app=app)
   589→
   590→            # Check the system Python on the target system to see if it is
   591→            # compatible with Briefcase, and that the required system packages
   592→            # are installed.
   593→            if verify_python:
   594→                self.verify_system_python()
   595→                self.verify_system_packages(app)

   597→        # Establish Docker as app context before letting super set subprocess
